reason_codes.rule-present: A verified Rootform rule accounts for this provider type.
reason_codes.composition-member: A verified composition retains this provider type as a proven composition member rather than an independent service root.
reason_codes.partial-rule: Verified Rootform semantics cover only the researched architecture role of this provider type.
reason_codes.no-rule: Provider declaration can be received, but no verified Rootform rule models it.
reason_codes.input-surface-not-modeled: Provider input surface can be authored, but Rootform has no accepted semantic handling for it.
reason_codes.provider-function-not-architecture: Provider-defined function is expression behavior, not an architecture declaration.
reason_codes.resource-identity-protocol-metadata: Resource identity schema is provider protocol metadata, not a Terraform declaration.
reason_codes.no-provider-surface: Dated Google Cloud catalog product has no matching declaration surface in either baseline provider.
reason_codes.provider-surface-unmodeled: Catalog product has baseline provider declarations, but none has verified Rootform semantics.
reason_codes.provider-surface-rule-present: Every researched independent architecture construct for this catalog product has verified Rootform semantics.
reason_codes.provider-surface-partially-modeled: Catalog product has at least one verified semantic construct, without claiming complete product coverage.
reason_codes.provider-surface-no-rule: Catalog product has provider surface but no independent architecture identity beyond modeled services or unmodeled configuration.
reason_codes.provider-surface-primitive-gap: Catalog product retains a researched architecture construct that current Rootform primitives cannot model honestly.
reason_codes.researched-architectural-gap: Research identifies an independent architecture construct, but no verified Rootform rule models it.
reason_codes.unmodeled-configuration-no-rule: Research classifies this provider resource as helper or configuration; without a semantic rule it remains explicit unmodeled input.
reason_codes.researched-unmodeled-configuration: Provider-only research classifies this declaration as configuration supporting an already modeled architecture construct.
reason_codes.researched-no-independent-architecture-v: Provider-only research finds no honest independent architecture identity for this declaration.
reason_codes.researched-provider-primitive-gap: Provider-only research identifies architecture meaning that current Rootform primitives cannot represent honestly.

family_evidence.architectural_role: managed conversational, document, discovery, Vertex AI, notebook, and blockchain runtimes
limitations: Model deployments, tools, flows, indexes, data stores, and endpoints create no inferred data flow without exact accepted evidence.

family_evidence.architectural_role: managed API gateways, Apigee runtimes, and Cloud Healthcare API stores
facts: healthcare store ownership in an exactly referenced dataset
limitations: API deployment revisions, policies, credentials, and integration clients remain configuration unless a runtime identity is explicit.
Literal network names do not prove a VPC context; an instance can also be bare metal.

family_evidence.architectural_role: GKE cluster with contributing node pools
limitations: No Kubernetes-provider ownership is inferred from provider configuration.

family_evidence.architectural_role: BigQuery dataset containing tables and access details
limitations: google_bigquery_model has no provider 8.0.0 surface and is not a Rootform-supported provider construct.

family_evidence.architectural_role: Cloud SQL instance with private services access support
facts: private reachability to an explicitly referenced VPC network
limitations: Private Service Connect is not renamed or inferred as private services access.
Repository format does not prove producer or consumer data flow.

family_evidence.architectural_role: Cloud DNS managed zone with contributing record sets
facts: record-set contribution to exact managed zone
limitations: No public or private visibility is inferred when configuration omits it.

family_evidence.architectural_role: Google Cloud API enablement on a project
limitations: API enablement is retained as supporting service detail, not promoted to a standalone architecture service.

family_evidence.architectural_role: distributed Kubernetes fleets, Oracle Database infrastructure, and VMware Engine private clouds
limitations: Fleet membership, node pools, provider-specific networks, and clusters share only identities proven by their declarations.

family_evidence.architectural_role: service account with project IAM access details
facts: member and binding contributions to every exactly referenced service account
limitations: Policy bodies and private service-account key material do not enter Architecture IR.
Standalone health checks and certificates are not rendered as load balancers; only a complete HTTPS proxy, URL map, and backend chain composes.
No producer is inferred from Terraform dependency evidence alone.

family_evidence.architectural_role: database and storage transfer jobs with supporting connection and agent resources
limitations: Source and destination strings do not create architecture relations without exact reference resolution.
Shared VPC host and service project roles remain unmodeled because neither declaration identifies one network.
Metric and log filter strings do not identify monitored architecture objects.

family_evidence.architectural_role: Secret Manager secret hierarchy and Cloud KMS key hierarchy
limitations: Secret data and cryptographic material never enter Architecture IR.

family_evidence.architectural_role: Cloud Run service and Cloud Run job
limitations: Only explicit Direct VPC network-interface references emit contexts.

family_evidence.architectural_role: Cloud Storage bucket with access detail
facts: IAM member contribution to exact bucket
limitations: Terraform dependencies do not create data-flow relations.
